studies.label: RIVAL 2020, JAMA Surg
studies.appraisal: Pilot with no primary outcome; patient-blinded only; 30-day follow-up; underpowered; same patients as the 2023 report.
studies.key_results: Median operative time 75.5 min with robotic vs 40.5 min with laparoscopic repair; median cost $3258 vs $1421; no difference in pain, SF-36, wound events or readmissions [32186683].

studies.label: RIVAL 2-year, Surg Endosc 2023
studies.appraisal: Same trial as RIVAL 2020; 77 of 102 completed 2-year follow-up; too few events to assess recurrence.
studies.key_results: Recurrence 1 with robotic vs 1 with laparoscopic repair at 2 years (P=1.0); pain, QoL and physical activity similar; no neuropathic pain [35578051].

studies.label: ROGER 2025, Br J Surg
studies.appraisal: Powered for 24-h pain; blinding for 7 days only; comparator TEP, not TAPP; baseline imbalance; surgeons more proficient in TEP; 1-year follow-up.
studies.key_results: Pain coughing at 24 h median 4 with rTAPP vs 5 with TEP (P=0.431); complications 9 (10%) vs 10 (11%); unilateral time 80.3 vs 64.2 min; cost $3327 vs $2732 [41511872].

studies.label: ROLAIS 2025, Br J Surg
studies.appraisal: Open-label; CRP primary outcome; 11 unbalanced pre-surgery withdrawals; same trial as DIRECT; high laparoscopic complication rate.
studies.key_results: Complications 23.0% with R-TAPP vs 41.5% with L-TAPP; operating time -13.4 min; same-day discharge 95.9% vs 81.5%; no difference in chronic pain or recurrence [40277023].

studies.label: DIRECT 2025, Hernia
studies.setting: University hospital, Denmark; four expert surgeons
studies.appraisal: Secondary analysis of ROLAIS (same patients, not independent); complexity classified after allocation; timing unblinded.
studies.key_results: Operative time 51 min with r-TAPP vs 60 min with l-TAPP (simple hernias) and 72 vs 92 min (complex hernias) [40632168].

studies.label: AIIMS RCT 2026, Surg Endosc
studies.appraisal: Abstract only; 2:1 allocation; surgeon experience not reported; 4-week follow-up.
studies.key_results: No difference in VAS pain at 3, 6 or 12 h (MD 0.28, -0.16 and 0.32), rescue analgesia (20.6% robotic vs 17.9% laparoscopic), operative time (p=0.142) or return to activity (p=0.180) [42527734].

studies.label: VOLTAIRE 2025, Am J Surg
studies.appraisal: Abstract only; small; unequal arms; open-console robot; ergonomics primary; blinding not reported.
studies.key_results: Operative time 64.9 min with robotic vs 31.7 min with laparoscopic repair; resumed activity at 14 days 15 (39%) vs 1 (5%); REBA 3 vs 5 [40450465].

studies.label: Stray energy RCT 2023, Surg Endosc
studies.appraisal: Histological surrogate outcome; samples rather than patients analysed; small.
studies.key_results: Port-site thermal injury in 60% of robotic vs 49% of laparoscopic samples (p=0.548) [37580577].

studies.label: RCT meta-analysis 2026, Surg Endosc
studies.design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 7 RCTs
studies.appraisal: GRADE low to very low; pool includes secondary reports (RIVAL follow-up, ROLAIS/DIRECT) and one TEP comparator; overlaps the other reviews.
studies.key_results: Complications RR 0.76 (95% CI 0.49-1.17); chronic pain RR 0.53 (0.20-1.39) [42625069].

studies.label: TAPP RCT meta-analysis 2026, J Laparoendosc Adv Surg Tech
studies.appraisal: Abstract only; same trials as the other reviews; imprecise.
studies.key_results: Complications RR 0.89 (0.45-1.78); operative time MD +18.5 min (-8.4 to 45.5) [42927985].

studies.label: Mixed meta-analysis 2026, J Robot Surg
studies.appraisal: 17 of 18 cohorts observational; confounding; GRADE low to very low.
studies.key_results: Recurrence RR 0.32 (0.17-0.59); operative time MD +30.04 min; complications RR 1.68 (1.00-2.84) [42541618].

studies.label: Italian cost-utility 2025, Hernia
studies.appraisal: Model-based, not a trial; assumes equal recurrence; Spanish cost inputs; ignores robot acquisition and learning curve.

studies.label: R-TAPP vs L-TEP meta-analysis 2025, J Robot Surg
studies.design: Meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis, 6 studies
studies.appraisal: Abstract only; appears to include non-randomised studies; pain result comes from sensitivity analysis.
studies.key_results: Operative time MD 17.76 min longer with R-TAPP; pain MD -1.59 (-2.41 to -0.76) [41452528].

studies.label: Da Vinci Xi meta-analysis 2025, J Robot Surg
studies.appraisal: Only 3 RCTs; the time advantage appears only after removing one study; overlaps the other reviews.
studies.comparison: Da Vinci Xi r-TAPP vs l-TAPP
studies.key_results: Operative time MD 0.59 min (-23.67 to 24.85; I2 98%); any complication OR 0.84 (0.19-3.79) [41182506].

studies.label: Short-term RCT meta-analysis 2025, Hernia
studies.appraisal: 3 open-label RCTs; ROLAIS supplemented with DIRECT data; overlapping pool.
studies.key_results: Operative time MD +17.6 min (-20.7 to 55.9); complications RR 0.83 (0.34-2.03); readmission RR 0.71 [41384988].

outcomes.why: Consistent null results in blinded trials, but they are small, and the chronic pain estimate is imprecise.
outcomes.effect_text: There was no difference in early or late pain. In ROGER, median NRS pain while coughing at 24 h was 4 with rTAPP vs 5 with TEP (P=0.431) [41511872]. In the Indian RCT, VAS mean differences (robotic minus laparoscopic) were 0.28 (95% CI -0.34 to 0.90) at 3 h, -0.16 (-0.69 to 0.37) at 6 h and 0.32 (-0.15 to 0.79) at 12 h [42527734]. Rescue analgesia was needed by 20.6% with robotic vs 17.9% with laparoscopic repair [42527734]. RIVAL found similar pain at 30 days, 1 year and 2 years [32186683; 35578051]. For chronic pain, the pooled RR was 0.53 (95% CI 0.20-1.39) from 2 RCTs [42625069].
outcomes.rct_evidence: ROGER, Indian AIIMS RCT, RIVAL (2020 and 2023 reports of one trial), meta-analysis of RCTs

outcomes.why: Inconsistency (ROLAIS vs the other trials), imprecision, and open-label design in ROLAIS.
outcomes.effect_text: Pooled RCTs show no significant difference in complications (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.49-1.17) [42625069]. Other RCT meta-analyses agree: RR 0.89 (0.45-1.78) [42927985] and RR 0.83 (0.34-2.03) [41384988]. In ROGER, complications occurred in 9 patients (10%) with rTAPP vs 10 (11%) with TEP [41511872]. In ROLAIS, open-label, complications were 23.0% with R-TAPP vs 41.5% with L-TAPP, and haematomas 6.8% vs 18.5% [40277023]. Port-site thermal injury occurred in 60% of robotic vs 49% of laparoscopic samples (p=0.548) [37580577].
outcomes.rct_evidence: ROGER, ROLAIS, RIVAL, stray-energy RCT; RCT meta-analyses (overlapping pools)

outcomes.why: Very few events, short follow-up and attrition; the only favourable signal is observational.
outcomes.effect_text: In RIVAL at 2 years there was 1 recurrence with robotic vs 1 with laparoscopic repair (P=1.0) [35578051]. ROLAIS and ROGER found no difference [40277023; 41511872]. A mostly observational meta-analysis reported RR 0.32 (95% CI 0.17-0.59) favouring robotic repair; this is non-randomised and not causal [42541618].

outcomes.why: Inconsistent results; small, partly unblinded trials, and a secondary outcome in VOLTAIRE.
outcomes.effect_text: In VOLTAIRE, more robotic patients had resumed normal activity at 14 days: 15 (39%) with robotic vs 1 (5%) with laparoscopic repair (p=0.006) [40450465; 42625069]. The blinded Indian RCT found no difference in time to resumption of activities (p=0.180) [42527734]. RIVAL found similar physical activity at 1 and 2 years [35578051].

outcomes.why: Two small trials with consistent null results; imprecise.
outcomes.effect_text: In ROGER, EQ-5D-5L at 12 months was 0.95 with rTAPP vs 0.96 with TEP (P=0.617) [41511872]. RIVAL found no SF-36 difference at 30 days, 1 year or 2 years [32186683; 35578051].

outcomes.why: Severe inconsistency (I2 about 98%), likely driven by surgeon experience.
outcomes.effect_text: Robotic repair was longer in three trials: median 75.5 min with robotic vs 40.5 min with laparoscopic TAPP [32186683]; 80.3 min with rTAPP vs 64.2 min with TEP [41511872]; 64.9 min with robotic vs 31.7 min with laparoscopic [40450465]. It was shorter in ROLAIS (-13.4 min) [40277023] and its DIRECT analysis (simple hernias 51 vs 60 min, robotic vs laparoscopic) [40632168]. The Indian RCT found no difference (p=0.142) [42527734]. Pooled RCTs give MD +18.5 min (95% CI -8.4 to 45.5; I2 97.7%) [42927985] and MD +17.6 min (-20.7 to 55.9; I2 98.8%) [41384988].
outcomes.rct_evidence: RIVAL, ROGER, VOLTAIRE, ROLAIS/DIRECT (one trial), Indian AIIMS RCT; RCT meta-analyses

outcomes.why: Consistent direction in two RCTs, but only two trials, and costs are setting-specific.
outcomes.effect_text: Median cost was $3258 with robotic vs $1421 with laparoscopic TAPP [32186683]. Mean unilateral procedural cost was $3327 with rTAPP vs $2732 with TEP [41511872]. An Italian model estimated an incremental cost of €2,224 for 0.05 QALYs gained, an ICER of €44,480/QALY, with under 25% probability of cost-effectiveness at €30,000/QALY [41258567]. This model is not trial-based and ignores robot acquisition and learning-curve effects.
outcomes.rct_evidence: RIVAL, ROGER; Italian model-based cost-utility analysis

outcomes.why: Single open-label trial; the other data are observational.
outcomes.outcome: Same-day discharge and length of stay
outcomes.effect_text: In ROLAIS, same-day discharge was 95.9% with R-TAPP vs 81.5% with L-TAPP (P=0.012) [40277023]. Mostly observational data show no significant difference in length of stay (MD +0.33 days, 95% CI -0.03 to 0.70) [42541618].

outcomes.why: Inconsistent results, unblinded surgeon-reported measures and different comparators.
outcomes.effect_text: Results are mixed. In RIVAL, frustration was higher with robotic repair (32.7 vs 20.1 with laparoscopic) [32186683]. In ROGER, NASA-TLX workload was 18.4 with rTAPP vs 34.0 with TEP [41511872]. In VOLTAIRE, median REBA ergonomic score was 3 with robotic vs 5 with laparoscopic repair [40450465].

conflicts.text: ROLAIS (with its DIRECT secondary analysis, one trial) found fewer complications (23.0% robotic vs 41.5% laparoscopic) and shorter operating time with robotic TAPP [40277023; 40632168]. RIVAL and ROGER found no complication difference and longer robotic operating time [32186683; 41511872]. The difference may reflect ROLAIS's open-label design, its CRP primary outcome, its unusually high laparoscopic complication rate, unbalanced withdrawals, and very experienced robotic surgeons (at least 100 r-TAPP each) [40277023; 40632168].

A mostly observational meta-analysis (17 of 18 cohorts observational) reported lower recurrence with robotic repair (RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59) [42541618]. The RCTs show no difference, with only 1 recurrence per arm at 2 years in RIVAL [35578051; 42625069]. The observational signal is prone to confounding and is not causal.

A meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis found lower pain with robotic TAPP than laparoscopic TEP (MD -1.59, 95% CI -2.41 to -0.76) [41452528]. Its pool appears to include non-randomised studies, and the finding comes from sensitivity analysis. It conflicts with the blinded ROGER RCT, which compared the same approaches and found no pain difference [41511872].

VOLTAIRE found more robotic patients back to normal activity at 14 days [40450465; 42625069]. The blinded Indian RCT found no difference in time to resumption of activities (p=0.180) [42527734]. VOLTAIRE was small, unequally allocated, used an open-console robot and had ergonomics as its focus [40450465].

Pooled operative-time estimates range from no difference (MD 0.59 min) to clearly longer robotic surgery (MD +30.04 min), with I2 around 98% [41182506; 42541618; 42927985; 41384988]. The spread is driven by trial design and surgeon experience. The largest pooled estimate (+30.04 min) is mostly observational [42541618].

at_a_glance.verdict: Robotic repair has not been shown to improve pain, complications, recurrence or quality of life over laparoscopic repair; it costs more and usually takes longer (low certainty).

key_numbers.label: Pain coughing at 24 h
key_numbers.value_text: median NRS 4 with rTAPP vs 5 with TEP, P=0.431 [41511872]

key_numbers.label: Median cost
key_numbers.value_text: $3258 with robotic vs $1421 with laparoscopic TAPP, P<.001 [32186683]

key_numbers.label: Operative time
key_numbers.value_text: 75.5 min with robotic vs 40.5 min with laparoscopic (median), P<.001 [32186683]

at_a_glance.main_caveat: a few small trials with experienced surgeons and short follow-up, underpowered for recurrence and chronic pain; one open-label trial (ROLAIS) found fewer complications with robotic repair [40277023].

bottom_line.text: Randomised trials show no consistent benefit of robotic over laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair for pain, complications, recurrence, quality of life or return to activity, while robotic repair costs more per case and usually takes longer [32186683; 35578051; 41511872; 42527734; 42625069]. The one trial favouring robotic repair (ROLAIS/DIRECT, fewer complications and shorter time) was open-label and single-centre [40277023; 40632168]. The trials are underpowered for recurrence and chronic pain, so equivalence on these outcomes cannot be claimed [42625069].
bottom_line.certainty_reason: Few small, mostly single-centre trials with short follow-up; inconsistent operative-time results; imprecise for rare outcomes.

would_change: A large multicentre blinded RCT powered for chronic pain and recurrence with at least 2-3 years of follow-up.
An independent trial replicating the ROLAIS complication and operative-time advantage with experienced robotic surgeons.
RCTs in obese patients and in recurrent or bilateral hernias, and studies of the robotic learning curve.
Trial-based cost-effectiveness analyses including robot acquisition and maintenance costs, especially from India or similar health systems.

applicability.case_mix: The randomised evidence covers mostly elective, uncomplicated, primary unilateral (some bilateral) inguinal hernias in predominantly male adults, operated on by experienced minimally invasive surgeons [32186683; 41511872; 42527734; 40277023]. ROGER excluded recurrent hernias [41511872]. The Indian trial enrolled uncomplicated hernias only [42527734]. There are no dedicated randomised data for obese patients, recurrent or bilateral hernias, or the robotic learning curve [42625069]. Most trials compared robotic TAPP with laparoscopic TAPP, but ROGER's comparator was laparoscopic TEP and VOLTAIRE used an open-console robot [41511872; 40450465].
applicability.training: The Italian model suggests confining r-TAPP to training programmes [41258567]. Surgeon workload findings are mixed: frustration was higher with robotic repair in RIVAL [32186683], while NASA-TLX workload was lower with rTAPP than TEP in ROGER [41511872] and ergonomic risk was lower in VOLTAIRE [40450465]. No RCT has assessed the robotic learning curve. ROGER's authors acknowledge that some rTAPP surgeons may not have completed it [41511872].
applicability.india_cost_context: One blinded single-centre RCT from AIIMS, India found no difference in early pain, rescue analgesia, operative time or return to activity [42527734]. That trial reported no cost data. All cost figures come from the US, Switzerland and an Italian model, all showing higher robotic cost per case [32186683; 41511872; 41258567]. Indian per-case costs, robot acquisition and maintenance costs, and the cost-effectiveness of robotic repair in Indian hospitals are not known from this evidence. The modelled analyses do not capture robot acquisition or learning-curve effects.

notable_findings.text: DIRECT, labelled an RCT, is a secondary analysis of the ROLAIS CRP trial on the same patients; allocation was by the surgeon on the day of surgery and hernia complexity was classified intraoperatively after allocation [40632168].
ROLAIS had 11 withdrawals before surgery with unbalanced arms (74 robotic vs 65 laparoscopic analysed) and was open-label [40277023].
RIVAL was a pilot with no primary outcome; only 77 of 102 patients completed 2-year follow-up, and the 2020 and 2023 reports describe the same patients [32186683; 35578051].
ROGER's rTAPP arm had more lateral and larger hernias, and its surgeons were more proficient in TEP, the institutional standard [41511872].
No guideline addressing robotic vs laparoscopic inguinal repair was found, and no included report states its funding or conflicts of interest [42625069].

clinical_practice.counselling: Expect similar pain, recovery, complication and recurrence risk with either approach; robotic surgery usually takes longer and costs more, and long-term data are limited [35578051; 41511872; 42527734].
clinical_practice.cost_per_case: Robotic repair costs roughly USD 595 more (Switzerland, rTAPP $3327 vs TEP $2732) to USD 1837 more (US, robotic $3258 vs laparoscopic TAPP $1421) per case [41511872; 32186683]; the Italian public-payer model gives an incremental cost of €2,224 [41258567]; Indian costs are not known.
clinical_practice.default_choice: Laparoscopic (TAPP or TEP) repair; robotic repair offers no proven patient benefit and costs more [32186683; 41511872; 42625069].
clinical_practice.who_may_benefit: The evidence does not identify any patient group; benefits in obese patients and in recurrent or complex hernias are untested in RCTs, and the only trial favouring robotic repair involved highly experienced robotic surgeons [40277023; 40632168].

ma_notes.text: Pooled 18 cohorts and 78,940 participants, mostly observational; the recurrence RR 0.32 is non-randomised.
The pool of 6 studies for r-TAPP vs laparoscopic TEP appears to include non-randomised studies, since the abstract recommends further randomized trials.
Counts 7 RCTs reported in 9 publications, so the pool includes secondary reports and overlapping trials such as RIVAL follow-up and ROLAIS/DIRECT; the pool also mixes TAPP and TEP comparators.
Pools only 3 RCTs; the operative-time advantage emerges only after removing the heterogeneity-driving study (I2 98%).

overlaps.note: RIVAL 2020 and its 1-2 year follow-up report the same 102 patients.
DIRECT is a secondary analysis of the ROLAIS trial (138 vs 139 patients), so they are a single trial.
The meta-analyses pool the same small set of RCTs and are not independent confirmations.

extract_next.text: Robotic TAPP vs laparoscopic TEP meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis; its pain-benefit claim conflicts with the RCTs and its pool composition needs checking.
GRADE-assessed RCT-only meta-analysis of r-TAPP vs l-TAPP; the operative-time result depends on removing one study.
RCT-only meta-analysis on short-term outcomes; useful for checking trial overlap and the consistency of the pooled operative time.

must_mention: Randomized evidence is small and low to very low certainty, with about 100-180 patients per trial, experienced surgeons and mostly uncomplicated hernias in men. Equivalence cannot be claimed for rare outcomes such as recurrence or chronic pain.
RIVAL was an underpowered pilot with no primary outcome and 25% loss to follow-up at 2 years. RIVAL 2020 and 2023 are the same patients.
ROLAIS and DIRECT are the same trial and are not independent. ROLAIS reported fewer complications and shorter operative time but was single-centre and open-label.
Comparators are heterogeneous: ROGER compared robotic TAPP with laparoscopic TEP, VOLTAIRE used an open-console robot, and the Indian RCT used 2:1 allocation.
Operative time results are inconsistent across trials (robotic longer in RIVAL, VOLTAIRE and ROGER, shorter in ROLAIS) with I2 around 98%.

Cost evidence is a model-based Italian cost-utility analysis (ICER €44,480/QALY) plus RIVAL cost data ($3258 vs $1421); no RCT-based cost-effectiveness analysis exists, and it ignores robot acquisition and learning-curve effects.

The lower-recurrence signal comes from observational data and should not be treated as causal. No guideline addressing robotic vs laparoscopic inguinal repair was found. No RCT data exist on obesity, recurrent or bilateral hernias, or the learning curve.

contradicting.text: Single-centre open-label RCT found robotic TAPP gave fewer complications, shorter operating time and more same-day discharge, which conflicts with a 'no difference' conclusion
contradicting.quote: R-TAPP was associated with a shorter operating time (-13.4 min, P < 0.001), fewer complications (23.0% versus 41.5%, P = 0.029), including fewer haematomas (6.8% versus 18.5%, P = 0.043), and a higher same-day discharge rate (95.9% versus 81.5%, P = 0.012).

contradicting.text: Pooled mostly non-randomised data show lower recurrence with robotic repair
contradicting.quote: robotic repair was associated with a lower observed recurrence risk (RR 0.32, 95% CI 0.17-0.59; I2 = 0%), although certainty was low and the randomized evidence was imprecise.

contradicting.text: Trial sequential analysis suggests lower postoperative pain with robotic TAPP versus laparoscopic TEP
contradicting.quote: Sensitivity and trial sequential analyses suggested a significant reduction in postoperative pain with R-TAPP, with TSA confirming robust evidence for lower pain scores

gaps.text: No differences between groups at preoperative, 1-week or 30-day points in wound events, readmissions, VAS pain or SF-36 quality of life.
gaps.outcome: Pain, quality of life, wound events and readmissions

Health-related quality of life and physical activity were similar at 1 and 2 years.

question: Does robotic inguinal hernia repair improve pain, complications, recurrence, return to normal activity, or quality of life compared with conventional laparoscopic repair? Assess randomized evidence, operative time, and costs.

added_outcomes.outcome: Specific complications: seroma, haematoma, infection, conversion, readmission
added_outcomes.effect_text: Pooled RCT estimates for specific complications showed no significant difference for r-TAPP vs l-TAPP: seroma RR 0.40 (95% CI 0.08-2.03), haematoma RR 0.65 (0.12-3.41) and surgical site infection RR 0.33 (0.03-3.14) [42927985 as 10]. Conversion RR was 1.00 (0.09-10.91) [10]. In the three-RCT Da Vinci Xi pool, haematoma OR was 0.64 (0.08-5.30), and readmission OR 0.51 (0.02-12.14) [14]. Readmission RR was 0.71 (0.09-5.58) in the short-term RCT pool [15].

notable_code.text: Not independent evidence (the skeptic): RIVAL 2020 and its 1-2 year follow-up report the same 102 patients.
Not independent evidence (the skeptic): DIRECT is a secondary analysis of the ROLAIS trial (138 vs 139 patients), so they are a single trial.
Not independent evidence (the skeptic): The meta-analyses pool the same small set of RCTs and are not independent confirmations.
What a meta-analysis pooled (the skeptic): Pooled 18 cohorts and 78,940 participants, mostly observational; the recurrence RR 0.32 is non-randomised.
What a meta-analysis pooled (the skeptic): The pool of 6 studies for r-TAPP vs laparoscopic TEP appears to include non-randomised studies, since the abstract recommends further randomized trials.

What a meta-analysis pooled (the skeptic): Counts 7 RCTs reported in 9 publications, so the pool includes secondary reports and overlapping trials such as RIVAL follow-up and ROLAIS/DIRECT; the pool also mixes TAPP and TEP comparators.
What a meta-analysis pooled (the skeptic): Pools only 3 RCTs; the operative-time advantage emerges only after removing the heterogeneity-driving study (I2 98%).
